title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues §1 of Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. C is the 'crystalline' or infinitesimal category of S relative to R: nilpotent thickenings S→T over R. A crystal of type F is a cartesian section of the fibred category F over C.

(1.5, Example 1, continued.) Take S = Spec k with k perfect, R = Spec Z, and W the Cohen ring of k. By Cohen's structure theory (W is formally smooth, and rigid because k is perfect), C is equivalent to the opposite of the category of local W-algebras A that are killed by a power of the maximal ideal of W and have residue field exactly k. Write W = lim W_n.
- If char k = p > 0, the W_n form a final family. An absolute crystal of modules is then a p-adic projective system (M_n) of W_n-modules with M_{n+1} ⊗ W_n ≅ M_n. Finitely presented crystals correspond to finitely generated W-modules (by p-adic completeness and noetherianity of W).
- If char k = 0 and k is algebraic over Q, then W = k. Spec k is ind-étale over Z, so every thickening is trivial, and crystals are just k-vector spaces.
- These identifications are compatible with base change in k and hold for any fibred category F.
- Under this dictionary the 'value at S' functor is M ↦ M ⊗_W k. For p > 0 it is not faithful: for example, multiplication by p on W is a nonzero map sent to 0. This illustrates the warning of 1.4 that a crystal is not merely a module with extra structure.

(1.6, Example 2.) If S is étale over R, then S itself (with the identity thickening) is final in C, by the infinitesimal lifting property of étale maps. Hence 'value at S' is an equivalence between crystals of type F and F_S. For modules, crystals are quasi-coherent O_S-modules. In particular, crystals of modules on Spec Z (absolute) are Z-modules.

(1.7, Example 3.) Let S be a subscheme of R. Crystals do not change if R is replaced by an open subscheme in which S is closed. So assume S = V(J) with J quasi-coherent, and set S_n = V(J^{n+1}), the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of S in R. The S_n form a final family in C (at least locally, for thickenings of bounded nilpotence order). Hence a crystal is a compatible system (M_n) with M_n ∈ F_{S_n}. If R is locally noetherian, finitely presented crystals of modules are coherent modules on the formal completion of R along S.

The next page notes two things. First, Example 1 in characteristic p is a special case of Example 3, via Cohen (absolute crystals on k are crystals relative to W). Second, Examples 2 and 3 unify for S→R unramified, which still admits infinitesimal neighbourhoods. The aim is to calibrate the new notion of crystal against familiar objects (Witt-vector modules, formal completions) before comparing crystals with stratifications in 1.8.
errors: 'le n.ème voisinage infinitésimal de R dans S' is inverted: S_n = V(J^{n+1}) is the n-th infinitesimal neighbourhood of S in R.

After the correction 'Si S=R' → 'S étale sur R', the phrase 'la catégorie C admet R lui-même comme objet final' and 'valeur en R' should read S (the sentence was written for S=R and only partially corrected; the second paragraph of 1.6 states the étale case correctly).

'Si p = 0' is shorthand for char k = 0. The char-0 claim relies on the added hypothesis that k is algebraic over Q. Otherwise Spec k is not formally étale over Z and absolute crystals are not just k-vector spaces.

The finality of the family (S_n) in C holds only locally, or for thickenings whose ideal is nilpotent of bounded order (e.g. quasi-compact T). Arbitrary nilpotent thickenings of a non-quasi-compact S need not factor through a single S_n globally. This is a minor gap, harmless since crystals are local.

The equivalence 'finitely presented crystals ≃ f.g. W-modules' tacitly uses that M_n of finite presentation over W_n, with M_{n+1}/p^{n+1}... ≅ M_n, yields a finitely generated limit (W noetherian, p-adically complete). This is true but unstated.

ideas.what: Absolute crystals of modules over a perfect field k ≃ p-adic systems of W_n(k)-modules; finitely presented crystals ≃ finitely generated W(k)-modules; the value functor is ⊗_W k and is not faithful.
ideas.modern_name: Crystals on the crystalline/infinitesimal site of a perfect field; Dieudonné-module-type description
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter to Tate; 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', IHES notes 1966, in Dix exposés 1968); Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, exposé IX 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by Coates–Jussila); letter to Tate circulated and widely cited

ideas.what: Thickenings of Spec k (k perfect) ≃ local W-algebras killed by a power of the maximal ideal with trivial residue extension, via Cohen rings.
ideas.modern_name: Cohen structure theory / universal property of Witt vectors for perfect rings

ideas.what: For S étale over R, S is final in the infinitesimal category, so crystals are just objects of F_S (quasi-coherent modules).
ideas.modern_name: Triviality of crystals for formally étale morphisms
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (Dix exposés); SGA/EGA formal étaleness

ideas.what: For S closed in R (locally noetherian), the infinitesimal neighbourhoods S_n are final; finitely presented crystals relative to R are coherent modules on the formal completion of R along S.
ideas.modern_name: Crystals relative to an embedding ≃ coherent modules on the formal completion (infinitesimal site via completion)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966); later Hartshorne (algebraic de Rham cohomology via formal completions), Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, Dix exposés (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: These are the standard foundational examples of the 1966 letter to Tate and of 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', all well absorbed into Berthelot's crystalline cohomology. Nothing new beyond a minor slip (the S/R inversion) and a partially corrected sentence.
transcription_corrections: 'le n.ème voisinage infinitésimal de R dans S' is what the typescript says (an error by Grothendieck), not a transcription error; keep, but note the inversion.
The marginal correction above 1.6 reads 'S étale sur R.' replacing the bracketed 'Si S=R,'.
In 1.7 the struck-out heading reads 'Relations avec la notion d'objet stratifié/' followed by 'Exemple 3'; 'sous-[-objet de-] préschéma' corresponds to the struck-out 'objet de' (with a stray 'x').
In 'S_n=V(J^{n+1})' the S is a handwritten script/underlined S; 'quasi-cohérent' is hand-corrected in the image.
